newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: RPT - HEINEKEN EVACUATES SOME ZAIREAN PERSONNEL.
newsitem.headline: RPT - HEINEKEN EVACUATES SOME ZAIREAN PERSONNEL.

text.p: Dutch brewer Heineken has evacuated seven of its personnel from its brewery in Kisangani as rebels approach the Zairean town, the company said on Wednesday.
Seven of the plant's 165 workers had chosen to leave, Heineken said, and the brewery continued to operate at some ten percent of its capacity of some 400,000 hectolitres per year.

"Only part of the 165 people working at the Kisangani brewery are not original inhabitants of that region. Of those people, seven preferred to leave," spokesman Koos Woltjes said. Families of these employees had been evacuated earlier.
Woltjes said the Kisangani brewery did not employ any expatriates. "We only have expatriates in Kinshasa," he said, adding neither they nor their families had been evacuated.
Woltjes said Heineken's brewery based at Bukavu in eastern Zaire was also operating at a very reduced capacity.
"The security of the people is most important," he said.
Although Heineken's operations in the region are being hit hard by the continuing conflict, the brewer has said it has no plans to pull out of the area.
Heineken has been in central Africa for around 50 years.
